correctness.rationale: All best-response branches are valid on the exact positive domain. A necessary quadratic identity for any primitive two-cycle and a strict root bound exclude period two for c>=3-2sqrt(2). Coppel 1955 then forces every compact-interval orbit to converge. Uniqueness of the positive Nash point plus repulsion of zero gives global convergence. Below the threshold, the second iterate has a sign-changing zero away from the equilibrium, and the same quadratic and sum-square identities give exactly one unordered cycle. The symbolic script verifies the discriminant, evaluation, four best-response identities and rational test-cycle multiplier exactly; no finite computation substitutes for the general proof.

value.rationale: An exact sharp global convergence threshold answers the stated heterogeneity question for the original two-agent model. Proving all-seed convergence is a substantive improvement over a local multiplier calculation; algebraic exclusion of every prime period-two orbit gives a complete obstruction classification. The threshold includes the neutral boundary c=3-2sqrt2 and is falsified below it by an actual interior cycle. The result is not merely a new example or a parameter substitution.
